gloss: obligation; debt of gratitude; favor received

definitions.gloss: obligation; debt of gratitude; favor received
definitions.explanation: A deep sense of moral indebtedness to someone who has helped you. Implies a duty to reciprocate the kindness, rooted in the Japanese cultural value of mutual obligation.

examples.japanese: {恩義|おんぎ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じている→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧。
examples.english: I feel a debt of gratitude.

examples.japanese: ⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{大|おお}きな→大きな：02849_ookina⟧{恩義|おんぎ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: I owe my teacher a great debt of gratitude.

examples.japanese: ⟦{命|いのち}→命：02371_inochi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{救|すく}って→救う：02063_sukuu⟧⟦くれた→くれる：00724_kureru⟧{恩義|おんぎ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{一生|いっしょう}→一生：01728_isshou⟧⟦{忘|わす}れない→忘れる：00474_wasureru⟧。
examples.english: I will never forget the debt I owe to the person who saved my life.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{恩|おん}→恩：02550_on⟧ (kindness, favor) and {義|ぎ} (duty, righteousness). Refers to the moral obligation one feels toward someone who has provided significant help or kindness. A culturally weighted concept in Japan, where reciprocating favors is deeply important.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {恩義|おんぎ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じる→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧: to feel a debt of gratitude
- {恩義|おんぎ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧: to be indebted to
- {恩義|おんぎ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{報|むく}いる→報いる：12088_mukuiru⟧: to repay a debt of gratitude
- {恩義|おんぎ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{忘|わす}れる→忘れる：00474_wasureru⟧: to forget one's obligations
- {恩義|おんぎ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{受|う}ける→受ける：01215_ukeru⟧: to receive a favor

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{恩|おん}→恩：02550_on⟧: favor, kindness — the kindness itself, without the duty component
- ⟦{恩返|おんがえ}し→恩返し：11063_ongaeshi⟧: returning a favor — the act of repaying kindness
- ⟦{義理|ぎり}→義理：10891_giri⟧: social obligation — a broader concept of duty in social relationships, including those without personal gratitude

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japanese culture, {恩義|おんぎ} carries significant moral weight. Forgetting or ignoring an {恩義|おんぎ} is considered a serious character flaw. The concept appears frequently in historical dramas and stories about loyalty.
